chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, all from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you enter the state of Ihram, you must have God-consciousness, remember God frequently, and speak little except in goodness. Indeed, part of the perfection of Hajj and Umrah is that a person protects his tongue except from goodness, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said.
So whoever determines the performance of the Hajj therein, there shall be no obscenity nor immorality nor quarrelling during the Hajj.
And the obscenity is copulation, and the immorality is lying and insulting, and the quarrelling is the words of the man, 'No, by Allah!' and 'Yes, by Allah!'

And know that the man, when he swears with three oaths consecutively in one place while he is in Ihram, has quarrelled. Therefore, upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal) to be spilled, and he should give in charity with it. And when he swears one false oath, he has quarrelled, and upon him is blood to be spilled, and he should give in charity with it.

And he said: Guard against boasting, and upon you is piety that restrains you from disobeying Allah, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Then let them fulfil their needful acts, and let them be loyal to their vows and let them go round the Ancient House.'

Abu Abdillah said: From al-Tafath is that you speak while in your Ihram with ugly speech. So when you enter Mecca and circumambulate the House, and you speak with good speech, that becomes an expiation.
He said: And I asked him about the man who says, 'No, by my life!' and 'Yes, by my life!'. He said: This is not from the quarrelling. Rather, the quarrelling is 'No, by Allah!' and 'Yes, by Allah!'.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.التَّفَث: The needful acts or removing impurities, here referring to speech habits

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for speech and oaths during Hajj Ihram according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elaborates on the spiritual discipline of the Hajj pilgrim, defining 'rafath', 'fusq', and 'jidal' not merely as physical acts but as linguistic transgressions, specifically linking 'jidal' to the use of emphatic oaths like 'La wa-Allahi'. This hadith provides a nuanced legal distinction in Shia jurisprudence, clarifying that while boasting is discouraged, the specific prohibition of 'jidal' applies to certain oath structures, whereas good speech after Tawaf serves as expiation for prior bad speech. The text underscores the holistic nature of Ihram, where internal piety manifests through strict control of the tongue, reflecting the Quranic command to avoid quarreling during the pilgrimage.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin yahya, and Ibn Abu Umeyr, altogether from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When you wear Ihraam, so upon you is with the fearing of Allahazwj, and mentioning Allahazwj frequently, and scarcity of the speech, except with goodness, for it is from the completion of the Hajj and the Umra that the person protects his tongue except from goodness, just as Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Said. So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [2:197] The Hajj is (performed in) the well-known months; so whoever determines the performance of the Hajj therein, there shall be no obscenity nor immorality nor quarrelling during the Hajj. And the obscenity (is a reference to) the copulation, and the immorality is the lying, and the insulting, and the quarrelling, the words of the man, ‘No, by Allahazwj!’, and ‘Yes, by Allahazwj!’ And know, that the man, when he swears with three oaths sincerely, in one place and he is wearing Ihraam, so he has quarrelled. Therefore, upon him would be blood (of a sacrificial animal) to be spilled, and he should give in charity with it. And when he swears an oath once, falsely, so he has quarrelled, and upon him would be blood (of a sacrificial animal) to be spilled, and he should give in charity with it’. And heasws said: ‘Fear the pride and upon you is with the piety, refraining you from disobeying Allahazwj, for Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [22:29] Then let them fulfil their needful acts, and let them be loyal to their vows and let them go round the Ancient House (Kabah)’. Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘From Al-Tafas (التَّفَثِ) is that you speak while being in your Ihraam, with ugly speech. So when you enter Makkah and circumambulate the House (Kabah), you should speak with good speech, so that would be an expiation’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about the man who is saying, ‘No, by my life!’, and ‘Yes, by my life!’’. Heasws said: ‘This is not from the ‘quarrelling’. But rather, the quarrelling is (saying), ‘No, by Allahazwj!’, and ‘Yes, by Allahazwj!’’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya and ibn abu ‘Umayr all from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When you assume the state of Ihram you must maintain piety before Allah. You must speak of Allah very often, talk very little unless it is for good reasons, of the completion of al-Hajj and al-‘Umrah is safeguarding one’s tongue except in what is good. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said,
“Those who make al-Hajj obligatory upon themselves must take notice that there is no sexual relation, lying, abusing and swearing in al-Hajj.” [2:197]
Swearing means to say, “No, by Allah, yes, by Allah.”

One must take notice that when a man swears three times at one place in the state of Ihram, he has committed al-Jidal (swearing), and he must offer an animal offering and give it as charity. For swearing only once which is a lie, he has committed al-Jidal (swearing), he must offer an animal offering and give it as charity.’

He (the Imam) has said, ‘Avoid boastfulness and you must stay away from sins in disobedience to Allah; Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “Then you must remove the dirt away from you, fulfill your vows and perform Tawaf around the free House.’” [21:28]

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is of al-Tafath (dirt) to speak improper words. When you enter Makkah, perform Tawaf around the House and speak nice words, it will be expiation (for speaking improper words).’
I asked him (the Imam) about the man who says, ‘No, I swear by my life, yes, by my life.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘That is not swearing. Swearing is saying, ‘No, by Allah, yes, by Allah.’”
